source.title: Revisiting Spatial Invariance with Low-Rank Local Connectivity
source.authors: G. Elsayed; Prajit Ramachandran; Jonathon Shlens; Simon Kornblith

record.tranche_reason: Compares convolutional, locally connected, and partially relaxed local-connectivity architectures on image classification, using test accuracy to assess architectural inductive bias.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for architecture comparisons relevant to V3. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, optimizer effects, batch size, dropout, generalization-gap measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study tests spatial weight sharing within locally connected image architectures. It does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks as V3 requires. Local receptive fields remain present in both its convolutional and locally connected models, so these results do not isolate the contribution of local connectivity either. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the small-network experiments: partial relaxation of spatial invariance improves accuracy over ordinary convolution and vanilla locally connected layers. Add the authors' ImageNet qualification: parameter-matched wider ResNet-50 models match or outperform LRLC. Input-dependent combining weights are most useful for less aligned data.
record.recipe_differences: Compares convolution and local-connectivity architectures on image classification with standard gradient training, but evaluates partially relaxed connectivity rather than the specific fully connected comparisons in V3.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset and layer placement; input-dependent combining weights help on CIFAR-10, help little on MNIST, and reduce accuracy on CelebA. On ImageNet, a wider convolutional ResNet-50 matches or outperforms LRLC.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing only the third convolutional layer with a locally connected layer improves accuracy on MNIST and CelebA but reduces it on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of spatial weight sharing depends on dataset and layer placement when local receptive fields are retained.

fits_no_version.finding: Third-layer LRLC exceeds ordinary convolution on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CelebA, and also exceeds the corresponding vanilla locally connected models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlled partial relaxation of spatial weight sharing can improve image classification over both full sharing and unrestricted local filters in small networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The core comparisons are on three datasets using small networks. The study does not test fully connected networks as specified by V3, and its reported accuracies are not direct measures of training-to-test error gaps. ImageNet results use a different ResNet-50 setup and include augmentation and explicit regularization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from Table 2 or Table Supp.4 were required for the third-layer architecture comparison. Other layer placements, input-dependent LRLC variants, CoordConv, and ImageNet comparisons are omitted to keep extraction focused on the version's convolution-versus-local-connectivity comparison.

untested.parts: Paired random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error beyond the width needed for zero training error. Parameter-matched width comparisons do not establish this threshold or the post-threshold trend.

Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch; the contribution of local connectivity; fully connected networks learning sparse local connections; initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Controlled optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against alternative measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplementary CONVOLUTION (FC) model is still a convolutional network; it replaces global average pooling with a fully connected final layer. It is not a fully connected network comparator for V3. V3 concerns held-out error, so the absence of a training-to-test gap estimate is not the exclusion reason. Additional architecture comparisons are declared in rows_left_out and do not supply tests of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
It compares convolutional and locally connected layers, but does not test fully connected networks learning sparse local connections or networks initialized from trained convolutional weights.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: CONVOLUTION
rows.size_stated: 3 layers with 64 channels at each layer; local filters of size 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Train image classifier with convolutional layers and report test accuracy.
rows.note: Reference convolutional model; accuracy alone does not give a paired error-gap estimate.
rows.check: Accuracy is correctly transcribed, but there is no fully connected comparator for V3.

rows.subject: LOCALLY CONNECTED (3RD LAYER)
rows.size_stated: 3 layers with 64 channels at each layer; local filters of size 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Replace the third convolutional layer with a locally connected layer and report test accuracy.
rows.note: This locally connected variant has higher accuracy than the convolution reference.
rows.check: The value and baseline are correct. A locally connected third layer retains local receptive fields; its advantage over convolution does not reverse V3's convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison.

rows.subject: LRLC (3RD LAYER)
rows.size_stated: 3 layers with 64 channels at each layer; local filters of size 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Replace the third convolutional layer with a low-rank locally connected layer and report test accuracy.
rows.note: The partially relaxed local-connectivity model has higher accuracy than the convolution reference.
rows.check: The value and baseline are correct. LRLC is the study's proposed locally connected method, not a fully connected network; its performance advantage does not reverse V3.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The locally connected model has lower test accuracy than convolution (R5). The study does not compare a fully connected network trained from scratch.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MNIST and CelebA, locally connected third layer; all three datasets, LRLC third layer
reader_labels.reason: Locally connected models exceed convolution on MNIST and CelebA, and LRLC exceeds convolution on all three datasets, so the convolution advantage depends on dataset and degree of spatial invariance (R2–R3, R6, R8–R9).
